scenes.name: Gótico
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Término que Hannett aplicó a Joy Division y luego insulto para los epígonos, hasta que en 1982 los fans lo adoptan como estandarte frente a la excesiva luminosidad del new pop: glamour sepulcral, retorno de lo reprimido, emociones atemporales. Bauhaus («Bela Lugosi's Dead», 1979, el comienzo propiamente dicho; Peter Murphy, sex symbol heredero de Adam Ant y Bowie), The Birthday Party (el gótico americano de Nick Cave: «Release the Bats», Junkyard), Killing Joke («música de tensión», del funk de PiL a Black Sabbath, con un aura inquietante), The Cure (gótico light: Seventeen Seconds, Faith, Pornography). El club The Batcave (1982), el «positive punk», Southern Death Cult, Theatre of Hate, The Sisters of Mercy («¡Nosotros sí somos una banda de rock!»), el death rock de Los Ángeles y Kukl con Björk. Su deriva: coqueteos totalitarios y la conversión en versión postpunk del heavy metal (The Cult).

podcast.title: 2019 On-Stage Heart Attack
podcast.body: On August 12, 2019, Peter Murphy experienced a heart attack while playing a residency at a club in New York's Greenwich Village. During a soundcheck, he felt shortness of breath and severe pain in both forearms. Despite the pain, he finished the show, though it was a struggle. "On August 12th, 2019, Peter Murphy was playing a residency at a club in New York's Greenwich Village. When he started experiencing shortness of breath as he was doing a sound check, there was also severe pain in his left forearm. Then that pain enveloped both arms. He finished the show, but it was a slog."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: People Who (Almost) Died

podcast.title: Adrenaline as a Life-Saver
podcast.body: Doctors informed Peter Murphy that the adrenaline he experienced while performing on stage during his heart attack was likely what saved him from the heart attack killing him outright. "doctors said that the adrenaline of performing is what saved him from the heart attack killing him."

podcast.title: Financial Struggles in Turkey
podcast.body: By the mid-1990s, Peter Murphy faced financial difficulties in Turkey, as the costs of full-time Arabic study, combined with earnings from translating books and composing music for his wife's dance company, proved insufficient compared to his potential income from reuniting with his former bandmates. "Peter Murphy was running out of money in Turkey."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus

podcast.title: Hospitalization and Coma
podcast.body: After his August 2019 show, Peter Murphy fought for breath at his hotel overnight. The next morning, he called his manager, stating, "I think I might be dying." He was taken to Lennox Hill Hospital, diagnosed with a myocardial infarction (heart attack), and required two stents in his right coronary artery, ultimately ending up in a coma. "Murphy was taken to Lennox Hill Hospital where he was diagnosed with a myocardial infarction, heart attack. He needed two stents in his right coronary artery and he ended up in a coma."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: People Who (Almost) Died

podcast.title: Iconic Maxell Commercials
podcast.body: In 1981, Peter Murphy was chosen to appear in TV commercials for Maxell Cassettes, receiving 10,000 pounds for two shoots. He became the recognizable figure in the enduring magazine ads depicting a person sitting in a chair being "blown away" by music from a stereo, an image that remained in use for over 15 years. "The guy in the chair? That's Peter Murphy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus?

podcast.title: Nine Inch Nails as Opener
podcast.body: In the spring of 1990, Nine Inch Nails opened for Peter Murphy during a tour. This provided an early touring platform for Trent Reznor's band, during which they performed a cover of a Queen song and experienced growing frustrations with their record label, TVT. "In the spring of 1990, Trent went on the road as the opener for Peter Murphy and one of the songs in the nine-inch nail set list at that time was this cover of an old song by Queen."

podcast.title: Nine Inch Nails as Opening Act
podcast.body: During his tour to promote the "Deep" album, Peter Murphy introduced thousands of people to a then-little-known band from Cleveland, Nine Inch Nails, who served as his opening act. "he introduced thousands of people to his opening act. Little band out of Cleveland called Nine-inch Nails."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus

podcast.title: Pneumonia and Band Division
podcast.body: Peter Murphy became severely ill with pneumonia just before Bauhaus was scheduled to record their next album. This led to the rest of the band recording "Burning from the Inside" without him, a process that revealed they could work effectively independently and contributed to the internal split of Bauhaus into two factions: Peter Murphy and everyone else. "And then Peter got very sick with pneumonia, just as the group was scheduled to start recording their next album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus?

podcast.title: Post-Bauhaus Projects and Dali's Car
podcast.body: After Bauhaus splintered on July 5, 1983, Peter Murphy briefly formed the band Dali's Car, which released one album before he embarked on a solo career. "Peter Murphy briefly formed a band called Dali's Car, which lasted for one album before he went solo."

podcast.title: Relocation to Turkey - Study of Islam
podcast.body: In the spring of 1990, funded by the success of his "Deep" album, Peter Murphy moved his family to Turkey, where he began an intensive study of Islam and eventually converted to the faith, becoming a Muslim. "he began to study Islam, eventually becoming a Muslim."

podcast.title: Withdrawal to Turkey and Islam
podcast.body: In the early 1990s, Peter Murphy began to withdraw from Western society, moving his family to Turkey after the success of his 1990 album "Deep." There, he dedicated himself to studying Islam and eventually converted, financing his full-time Arabic studies and other pursuits through earnings from his music and other ventures, though these paled in comparison to potential reunion earnings. "In the spring of 1990, he released an album that sold enough copies to allow him to move his family to Turkey, where he began to study Islam, eventually becoming a Muslim."

xref.title: Band Breakup - Hammersmith Palais (1983)
xref.body: Bauhaus concluded their initial run with a final performance on July 5, 1983, at the Hammersmith Palais in London. The breakup was attributed to rising egos, creative differences, the pressures of touring, and Peter Murphy's severe bout of pneumonia, which forced the band to record an album without him, leading to internal divisions. "As the gig at the Hammersmith Pele came to an end, David J grabbed the mic and said, rest in peace. And that was that. Bajaos was dead."

xref.title: Internal Strife and Breakup
xref.body: The band's progress was halted by internal issues including egos, creative differences, and touring pressures. Peter Murphy's illness with pneumonia during the recording of their next album led to the rest of the band recording "Burning from the Inside" without him, which highlighted their ability to function independently and created a "battle of egos," leading to their eventual split. "Ego's got on the way. Creative differences, the pressures of touring. And then Peter got very sick with pneumonia, just as the group was scheduled to start recording their next album."

xref.title: Peter Murphy's Maxell Commercial - Iconic Ad Appearance
xref.body: In 1981, Peter Murphy was selected to appear in a TV commercial for Maxell cassettes, earning him 10,000 pounds. The iconic magazine ads based on these commercials, featuring a person in a chair being "blown away" by music, continued to be used for more than 15 years after their initial release. "The guy in the chair? That's Peter Murphy."

xref.title: Post-Bauhaus Success
xref.body: Formed by Daniel Ash, David J, and Kevin Haskins after Peter Murphy declined a Bauhaus reunion, Love and Rockets achieved greater commercial success than Bauhaus. They sold millions of records worldwide, headlined large tours, and secured a Top 40 hit in America. "Daniel Ash, David J and Kevin Haskins were far more successful than Bajaos could have ever been selling millions of records around the world, playing huge headline tours, and even having a top 40 hit in America."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Breakup Projects
xref.body: After the band Bauhaus "splintered," its members went on to form other significant groups, including Tones on Tail and Love and Rockets. Additionally, the individual members, Peter Murphy, David J, and Daniel Ash, pursued solo careers. "Bauhaus splintered into tones on tail and loving rockets and indirectly gave us Peter Murphy, David J and Daniel Ash."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Reconstitution as Love and Rockets
xref.body: After Tones on Tail ceased activity, the group was reconstituted under the name Love and Rockets, which featured the members of Bauhaus with the exception of singer Peter Murphy. This new iteration went on to have a successful run with multiple significant singles. "When Tons on Tale Lost Steam, the group was reconstituted under the name Love and Rockets, which was Bajaos minus singer Peter Murphy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Reunion Tour
xref.body: Fifteen years and four days after their last London show in 1983, Bauhaus reunited for a performance at the Hollywood Athletic Club, with Peter Murphy finally agreeing to a reunion after years of requests, capitalizing on the "80s retro craze." This successful gig was followed by several sellout shows at the Hollywood Palladium, where 7,000 tickets sold in just over 15 minutes, leading to a full-tilt reunion tour. "15 years and four days after that last show in London, Baha's appeared on stage at the Hollywood Athletic Club."
